newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom gain supports soggy NZ shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom gain supports soggy NZ shares at close.

text.p: * New Zealand shares end softly on moderate turnover
* Telecom gain helps partly offset weakness elsewhere
* Volatile trade in Fernz Corp, Trans Alta
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -2.79 at 2,368.03
349 -1 * NZSC cap index +7.43 at 5,106.12
338 -3 * NZMC .NZMC cap index -10.43 at 1,886.15
369 nil * Volume NZ$54 million. Futures untraded
719 +7 * Other movers - -4 -15
New Zealand shares ended with a marginally softer tone on Tuesday with a gain in Telecom mostly offsetting weakness in the other leading issues.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended just 2.79 points down at 2,368.03 on moderate turnover, worth NZ$54 million.
Had it not been for a seven-cent rise in Telecom to $7.19 the index would have been down about 10 points.
Telecom and Brierley Investments dominated turnover on the day, but Fletcher Forest, Paper and Carter Holt Harvey were also actively traded.
Fernz Corp fell again, this time by 15 cents to NZ$4.80, as initial enthusiasm about its latest push into France continued to dissipate.
Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said the move down appeared to be corrective.
TransAlta was also volatile, trading at a NZ$1.92-2.05 range before ending unchanged at NZ$2.00.
The company said earlier that it planned to buy into two power stations owned by its parent, TransAlta Corp in exchange for 25.2 million shares at $1.75/share.
Koller said the shares being issued at such a large discount helped push TransAlta's price around.
